subject: Renewal amendment: reserved GPU scale + spillover framework
messages:
From: Lara Mendes <lara@atlashealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Gabe Ortiz <gabe@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning: reserve 16 GPUs + overflow behavior

Hi Grace,

We're starting renewal planning and looking to increase our Reserved Dedicated pool from 8 -> 16 GPUs for Q4 onward. Our projections (attached) show a peak cadence in November that would exceed the new committed pool by ~40% for several short bursts.

Two asks as we prepare the renewal:
- Can Redwood commit to a throughput floor (tokens/sec) for the reserved pool and a clear SLO/monitoring for latency?
- How does the overflow/burst behavior work during renewal? We want to avoid sudden hard caps that block traffic—prefer an on-demand spillover model but need to understand throttles, preemption rules, and predictable overage pricing.

Also looping finance/procurement — procurement will start the PO when we confirm terms.

Thanks,
Lara

--
Lara Mendes
Director, Platform Operations
Atlas Health

Subject: Re: Renewal planning: reserve 16 GPUs + overflow behavior

Hi Lara — thanks for the forecast and heads-up. We're excited to support the expansion. High-level answer first, then I'll pull in engineering details and a clean amendment for signatures:

- Committed pool: we can support a change from 8 -> 16 reserved GPUs with a 24-month term or a 12-month term with a smaller discount.
- Throughput SLO: we can guarantee baseline throughput per-GPU (we'll include tokens/sec table), plus 1-min and 5-min latency SLOs tied to the reserved pool.
- Overflow: our recommended default is on-demand spillover to our shared capacity with automated routing and billing by overage tokens; we also offer a hard-cap option if you need strict spend control.

I'll work with Aditya and Dev to outline the technical guardrails (preemption behavior, throttling thresholds, notification windows). Attaching a draft amendment (v1) for initial review — will iterate after internal alignment.

Best,
Grace

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-30T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Renewal planning: reserved 16 GPUs + overflow behavior — technical note

Folks — technical summary and recommendations for the amendment:

Summary of options:
1) Soft spillover (recommended) — traffic beyond reserved pool automatically routed to on-demand hosts. Characteristics: pay-as-you-go overage, preemption only when shared capacity is constrained, notifications at 80%/95% of forecasted burst budget. Can include a burst credit bucket for controlled free bursts.
2) Hard cap — requests above reserved pool get a 429 or queued; predictable cost ceiling but potential customer-visible rejections during peak.
3) Hybrid (preferred compromise) — on-demand spillover with a configurable emergency hard cap that triggers only after sustained overflow (e.g., >10 minutes) or if spend exceeds a negotiated threshold.

Throughput SLOs and measurement: we can publish per-route median p50/p95 latency and provide a tokens/sec baseline (see attached table). Guarantee will be scoped to reserved pool capacity and measured at the route level; overflow latency will be best-effort but we can provide expected median and 95th percentiles for the on-demand path.

Preemption and fairness: on-demand hosts use priority routing. Reserved requests get top priority; spillover runs at lower priority and may be preempted by higher-tier customers. We'll include a policy that gives Atlas a mitigation window (notifications + 5 minute grace) before preemption during sustained contention.

Pricing guardrails: recommend setting an overage multiplier (x) for spillover billing and an emergency hard cap multiplier (y) for absolute protection. Suggested starting point: overage multiplier = 1.8x of reserved unit rate, emergency hard cap at 2.0x but configurable.

Recommendation: commit to 16 GPUs, 24-month term for a 12% discount, soft spillover with an emergency hard cap at 1.75x and a 45-day performance test window.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-03T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Revised amendment and pricing for 16 GPU reserved pool (v2)

Hi Lara / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a revised amendment (v2) reflecting the recommended approach from engineering:
- Committed capacity: 16 reserved GPUs starting 2026-11-01
- Term: 24 months (option for 12 months at reduced discount)
- Throughput guarantee: baseline tokens/sec per GPU and route-level latency SLOs (see SLA table)
- Overflow: default = on-demand spillover with overage billing (1.6x unit rate). Emergency hard cap available and will trigger only after sustained overflow (policy: sustained > 10 minutes or overage spend hits agreed threshold).
- Test window: 45-day operational validation after go-live; if Atlas is not satisfied, we will work through remediation credits and tuning.

Action items:
1) Review v2 and provide procurement redlines by COB Oct 6 so we can finalize pricing and start DocuSign.
2) If you prefer a stricter hard cap instead of spillover, let us know — we can price it but expect more conservative throughput SLAs.

DocuSign link is embedded in the doc; I'm happy to hop on a 30m call if needed.

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-06T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revised amendment and pricing for 16 GPU reserved pool (v2) — procurement redlines

Hi Grace —

We've reviewed v2 and have three primary redlines before procurement can issue the PO:
1) Reduce the overage multiplier to no more than 1.4x of the reserved unit rate.
2) Limit the maximum burst multiplier (emergency hard cap) to 1.5x instead of 1.75x or 2.0x.
3) Formalize a 30-day production test window (we prefer 30 days rather than 45) with explicit KPIs for latency and availability before final billing adjustments.

We attached the PO for reference. Also require an explicit preemption and eviction policy for spillover workloads (how long Atlas requests can run before being preempted, notification cadence).

If you can accept points 1–3 (or propose a small compromise), we'll sign and issue the PO this week.

Thanks,
Procurement Team

Attachment: atlas_po_1005123.pdf (PDF)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Lara Mendes <lara@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revised amendment and pricing for 16 GPU reserved pool (v2) — response to redlines

Hi all —

Appreciate the clear asks. After internal review we've put together a compromise that should align with operational risk and Atlas's procurement constraints:
- Overage multiplier: we can accept 1.5x (compromise between your 1.4x and our 1.6x).
- Burst multiplier / emergency hard cap: set at 1.75x but with an automated throttling behavior — sustained overflow beyond 10 minutes will first trigger progressive throttles and notifications; hard cap enforced only if overflow spend hits the agreed threshold. This preserves burst headroom while protecting against runaway spend.
- Performance test window: we'll shorten to 45 ->  thirty-five days instead of 30 to give both sides a bit more tuning time; however, we're willing to accept a 30-day billing hold if Atlas prefers.

Next steps: if Atlas accepts, we'll update the amendment and send a DocuSign link. Billing will provisionally start once DocuSign is complete and the reserved pool is provisioned on 2026-11-01. I'll also share the HubSpot deal and next-step checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Grace

--

Account Executive | Redwood Inference
